audit.why: Seastone Trident is Fizz's W; the slow and untargetability are Playful/Trickster (E, 16/14/12/10/8s). Chum the Waters is the R. Destiny is 170/140/110s, so the two-item row is where its cooldown stops mattering.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said Pick a Card is an auto-attack reset, and 'early' described the gold card as a skillshot landed from range.
audit.why: Pick a Card is a flat 6s and has range 200 — it empowers his next attack, so the tell is the attack wind-up, not the card lock, and it must connect in attack range. Playing around a phantom skillshot is the wrong dodge entirely.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d and content early now play around the wind-up and the melee range.

edits.before: Twisted Fate wins by landing Pick a Card (Gold), denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Twisted Fate wins by locking the gold card for his jungler's arrival, poking you off the wave, and Gating into every skirmish.

edits.before: Fish the strings and respect one spell — his CC is the lane; everything else is water.
edits.after: Fish the strings and respect one spell — the gold card is the lane; the rest is water.

edits.before: Shark the rivers: chip, R the entry, string the target, pole the response. One deletion per shark cycle.
edits.after: Chip with W bleed and hold the pole for the gold card — with no dash he cannot leave once you step in.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Check it before every step-up. - E Playful / Trickster is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card: matchup-defining — a flat 6s at every rank, so the gold card is never truly gone; back off the moment it glows yellow and step up on the blue. - Destiny is 170s at rank 1 and reveals you: his roam clock. - E Playful / Trickster is the lifeline.

edits.before: If Twisted Fate opens the score, reset expectations and respect Pick a Card (Gold) doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with W last-hits and stay relevant through pole plays.
edits.after: If Twisted Fate opens the score he prices you off the wave with Wild Cards — last-hit with W, stand where only one card can clip you, and step up the moment a gold is spent on a minion.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — shark, string, pole, repeat; one carry per fight is the contract and the pole notarizes it.
edits.after: Carry by hunting a mage with no dash — pole the gold card, then shark, string and delete him before Destiny returns.

edits.after: He fights as global vision and a Gate flank — shark his landing, string him down, and pole the gold card he saved for you.

edits.before: Ahead, fish openly: zone Twisted Fate with string threat, shark every river, and pole the counterplay — fed Fizz makes the map an aquarium.
edits.after: Ahead, take the map back: Destiny is 170s at rank 1, so punish every window it is down, shark him under tower and deny the vision game.

edits.before: Q through him, W bleed, walk out through the wave — the fish phases in and out before his answer finds a target.

edits.after: Once you hit level 3 your Playful/Trickster (E) slow lets you punish Twisted Fate's total lack of a dash every time he steps up to land a Wild Cards poke.

edits.before: Twisted Fate has no dash and no hard CC besides a gold-card stun that requires hitting a skillshot from range, so once you're level 3 you can walk up behind minions, land E for the slow, and chunk him before he can reposition. He'll try to poke with blue-card Wild Cards from max range, but his mana costs add up fast and he has zero disengage if you commit through minions. Punish every card he throws that isn't a guaranteed hit by immediately closing distance.
edits.after: Twisted Fate has no dash and no hard CC besides the gold card, which is an empowered attack he must land in attack range rather than a skillshot, so once you're level 3 you can walk up behind minions, hop the swing, and chunk him before he repositions. He'll poke with blue-card Wild Cards from max range, but his mana costs add up fast and he has zero disengage if you commit through minions. Punish every card he throws that isn't a guaranteed hit by immediately closing distance.

notes:

Both corrected. The 'early' paragraph also called Pick a Card a skillshot; it is range 200 and empowers his next attack, so the dodge is the attack wind-up, not a projectile.
